correctness.rationale: After affine normalization and vertical Steiner symmetrization, Lassak's support parameter is \(w\in[1,2]\). On the low branch the exact deficit factorization is strictly positive for every relevant \(w<2\). On the high branch \(f(w,z)=(w-2)q(w,z)\) and the completed-square identity gives \(q>0\) because the branch begins beyond \(8/7\); hence equality forces \(w=2\). At that endpoint the comparison polygon is the stated pentagon. Undoing Steiner symmetrization is rigid because its slice half-width is affine on each side of height zero; convexity/concavity force the slice center to be affine, and the three required hexagon slices fix it identically at zero. Exact rational checks confirm the algebra, area \(7\), and centroid \((0,4/21)\).
correctness.risk: The proof depends on Lassak's geometric comparison reductions; those reductions were checked against the primary article, while the new equality bookkeeping is supplied by the audited proof.

final_claim: Equality in Lassak's planar centroid bound \(g(A)\in o+\frac4{21}(H-o)\) for a convex body with an inscribed affine-regular hexagon is rigid: after cyclic relabeling the body is exactly the pentagon obtained by adjoining the corresponding outer star vertex, so there is one equality body up to affine equivalence.
limitations: No higher-dimensional analogue or quantitative stability theorem is claimed.
